prompt_text: What is the best Airbnb or short term rental to book in Nashville for a family of four?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on your dates, budget, where you want to be, and what your family needs. A few quick questions will let me give specific listing suggestions:

- When are you traveling (dates or month)?
- What’s your budget per night (or total)?
- Ages of the kids?
- Will you have a car / need parking?
- Do you want to be within walking distance of downtown attractions (Broadway, stadium) or prefer a quieter neighborhood vibe?

While you answer, here are practical recommendations and neighborhood picks so you know what to look for.

What to prioritize for a family of four
- Entire home or townhouse (2+ bedrooms, separate beds)
- Full kitchen and laundry (washer/dryer)
- Parking or easy ride-share access
- Quiet/child-friendly neighborhood (no party houses)
- Safety — good lighting, locks, smoke/CO detectors
- Host who provides crib/high chair or child supplies if needed
- Flexible cancellation for travel uncertainty

Best neighborhoods for families
- 12South: Walkable, lots of family restaurants, boutiques, parks. Great for a household feel (houses/cottages).
- Germantown: Quiet, close to downtown and easy access to riverfront/parks. Many renovated row-homes and condos.
- East Nashville: Artsy, residential, backyard space, playgrounds — very family-friendly vibe.
- The Gulch: Most central/walkable to downtown and dining, but pricier and more condo-style.
- Midtown/Vanderbilt: Close to museums, parks, and hospitals; convenient for concerts/sports.
- Green Hills / Belle Meade: Suburban, quieter, good if you want more space and shopping access (longer drives into downtown).

Where to search and filter tips
- Use Airbnb/Vrbo filters: “Entire place”, 2+ bedrooms, “Good for kids”, crib/high chair, free parking, washer/dryer.
- Sort by “Superhost” and read recent reviews for cleanliness and host responsiveness.
- Check the house rules for noise/party restrictions (important near downtown).
- Message the host before booking to confirm child items (crib, high chair) and parking details.

Typical property types to consider
- 2BR bungalow/house in 12South or East Nashville — backyard, family-friendly, walkable dining
- 2–3BR condo in Germantown or The Gulch — newer buildings, elevators, central access
- Townhouse near Vanderbilt — good for events/concerts and university visits

Price expectations (very rough, varies by season)
- Budget-friendly (off-peak): $120–200/night for a modest 2BR house or condo
- Mid-range: $200–350/night for nicely updated 2–3BR in popular neighborhoods
- Higher-end/central The Gulch: $350+/night for luxury condos or large houses

Other options
- Family suites at kid-friendly hotels (Hutton Hotel, Drury Plaza) if you want daily housekeeping and on-site help.
- Vrbo sometimes has more whole-house options in quieter neighborhoods.

If you tell me your dates, budget, and any must-haves (parking, crib, proximity), I’ll find 4–6 specific Airbnb/Vrbo-style property recommendations and explain the pros/cons of each.
